comment: Security advisories of eFa-next. Published signed with each release at https://repo.efa-next.eu/advisories/advisories.json (detached signature advisories.json.sig, repository key 1823D6D3BB7D5AEA286E836DCFE7E07916CC8046); the CVE watch of every host reads it. fixed: [epoch, version, release] of the first package with the fix; the release without the platform part (1, not 1.el9), so one entry fits EL9 and EL10 (1.el9 and 1.el10 both count as newer than 1).

advisories.summary: Web interface: multipart form bodies were parsed before a login without a limit on their parts (Werkzeug 2.0 of EL9); a client could tie up memory and CPU.
The rspamd repository file named http for packages and key; dnf could take a new key unasked. It is used only over https now.
An update of a set-up host without /etc/eFa-Version ran the first-install steps, which replaced its nginx, rspamd and Postfix settings.
A package update of 6.0.0.6 deleted the second factor (2FA) of the main admin of the web interface as a left-over row: the login took the password alone. Set up 2FA again after updating.
rspamd before 4.3.0: worker crash on crafted headers, use-after-free and out-of-bounds reads in the milter, ARC and Authentication-Results spoofing. Fixed by requiring rspamd 4.3.0.
Cluster nodes did not get the 2FA (TOTP, passkeys) of the logins from the master: on a node a user with 2FA on the master logged in with the password alone. The 2FA now goes to every node.
nginx flaws in HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and the mail proxy (CVSS 9.2). Mitigation only: 6.0.0.6.6.1 switches HTTP/2 of the web interface off; the fix is the nginx update of the OS vendor.
A cluster node could silently stop following its master (Fail2Ban busy): it then missed new bans, settings and 2FA changes. 6.0.0.6.6.2 keeps it following and alarms.
